tasks.title: Audit admin/agents.php layout against existing admin panel components
tasks.description: Conduct a comprehensive visual and code audit of the new admin/agents.php layout to identify discrepancies in containers, typography, spacing, and button styles compared to existing admin UI components, then prepare a detailed change list for alignment.
tasks.details:
1. Open admin/agents.php in browser and take screenshots of all sections
2. Compare with existing admin panel pages (dashboard, users, settings, etc.) to establish baseline UI patterns:
   - Container widths, margins, and padding standards
   - Typography hierarchy (h1, h2, h3, p, labels) and font sizes
   - Button styles, colors, hover states, and sizing
   - Form element styling and spacing
   - Table layouts and cell padding
   - Navigation and breadcrumb patterns
3. Document current admin/agents.php CSS classes and inline styles
4. Create detailed comparison matrix identifying specific discrepancies:
   - Container: wrapper divs, content areas, sidebar alignment
   - Typography: heading sizes, font weights, line heights, color values
   - Spacing: margins between sections, padding within elements
   - Buttons: primary/secondary styles, dimensions, border radius
5. Generate prioritized change list with specific CSS modifications needed
6. Include before/after mockups or annotated screenshots
7. Note any custom styling that should be preserved vs. standardized
8. Document recommended CSS class names to match existing admin conventions
tasks.testStrategy: Review change list with UI/UX team for completeness. Cross-reference identified discrepancies by viewing admin/agents.php alongside 3-4 other admin pages in split-screen mode. Validate that all major UI components (headers, forms, tables, buttons) are covered in the audit. Confirm change list includes specific CSS selectors and property values for each required modification.

subtasks.title: Capture current admin panel layout patterns
subtasks.description: Review admin/admin_panel.php and note container classes, card markup, spacing utilities, typography, and button styles that define the standard admin visual language.
subtasks.details:
<info added on 2025-11-09T12:18:10.697Z>
Established baseline admin styling patterns from admin_panel.php analysis:

Container Structure:
- Main wrapper: div.admin-panel-container.container-fluid.py-4.px-3.px-md-4 with max-width 1600px
- Custom font definitions in inline style block

Typography Hierarchy:

- Section headers: h2.h6.text-light.mb-0 or similar text-light headings
- Supporting text: text-light/text-muted combinations
- Emoji prefixes for section names (🔧 for Characters)
- Font references: --font-brand/body variables

Navigation Pattern:
- Container: div.admin-nav.row.g-2.g-md-3.mb-4
- Button wrapper: col-* responsive columns
- Button styling: nav-btn.btn.btn-outline-danger.btn-sm.w-100.text-center
- Active state: .active class application

Component Styling:
- Stats widgets: .stat-mini elements with gradient backgrounds, borders, centered typography
- Grid system: Bootstrap responsive columns (col-12 col-sm-4 col-lg-3)
- Cards/tables: dark gradient backgrounds with #8B0000 borders
- Consistent btn-outline-danger palette for all buttons
- Layout spacing: Bootstrap rows with g-* spacing and mb-4 margin utilities

These patterns will serve as the reference standard for agents.php refactoring to ensure visual consistency across the admin interface.

tasks.title: Implement Character Agent automation pipeline that processes Valley by Night characters directly from the MySQL database via includes/connect.php and writes outputs into agents/character_agent/reports/
tasks.description: Create an automated pipeline that connects to the MySQL database using the existing includes/connect.php connection, retrieves Valley by Night character data, processes it through the character agent system, and generates structured reports in the agents/character_agent/reports/ directory.
tasks.details:

   - Implement error handling for database connection failures

   - Extract character attributes (name, clan, generation, disciplines, etc.)
   - Format data into standardized structure for agent processing
   - Handle missing or null character data gracefully
   
3. Implement report generation system:
   - Create agents/character_agent/reports/ directory structure
   - Generate individual character analysis reports (JSON/HTML format)
   - Create summary reports aggregating character statistics
   - Implement timestamped file naming convention (YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS_character_report.json)
   
4. Add automation features:
   - Command-line interface for manual execution
   - Scheduling capability for automated runs
   - Progress tracking and logging system
   - Configuration file for customizable processing parameters
   
5. Database optimization:
   - Use prepared statements for secure queries
   - Implement pagination for large character datasets
   - Add indexing recommendations for performance
   
6. Error handling and logging:
   - Log all database operations and errors
   - Implement retry logic for failed operations
   - Create detailed error reports for troubleshooting

tasks.title: Update Page Links from index.php to character_sheet.php
tasks.description: Update all internal and external links, references, and redirects that point to index.php for character viewing to now point to character_sheet.php instead.
tasks.details:
1. Identify all files that contain references to index.php for character viewing:
   - Search through all PHP files, HTML files, and JavaScript files for references to index.php
   - Focus on links, form actions, redirects, and AJAX calls that specifically relate to character viewing

2. Update the following types of references:
   - HTML anchor tags: `<a href="index.php?character_id=123">` → `<a href="character_sheet.php?character_id=123">`
   - Form actions: `<form action="index.php" method="post">` → `<form action="character_sheet.php" method="post">`
   - PHP redirects: `header('Location: index.php?character_id=' . $id);` → `header('Location: character_sheet.php?character_id=' . $id);`
   - JavaScript/AJAX calls: `fetch('index.php?character_id='+id)` → `fetch('character_sheet.php?character_id='+id)`
   - Include/require statements if relevant: `include('index.php')` → `include('character_sheet.php')`

3. Pay special attention to these specific files:
   - player_dashboard.php (character links)
   - admin_dashboard.php (character management links)
   - Any navigation menus or sidebar components
   - Any JavaScript files that handle character viewing or editing
   - Any PHP files that process character data and redirect to the character sheet

4. Update any URL parameters or query strings while maintaining their functionality:
   - Preserve all GET parameters when updating URLs
   - Ensure any character_id, action, or other parameters remain intact

5. Check for any conditional logic that might reference the filename:
   ```php
   if (basename($_SERVER['PHP_SELF']) == 'index.php') {
       // Update this condition
   }
   ```

6. Document all changes made in a changelog for reference.
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Create a comprehensive test plan that covers all updated links:
   - Compile a list of all files modified and the specific changes made
   - For each modified file, test the functionality that involves links to character viewing

2. Test all navigation paths to character sheets:
   - From player dashboard to character sheet
   - From admin dashboard to character sheet
   - From character listings to individual character sheets
   - Any other navigation paths that should lead to character viewing

3. Test form submissions:
   - Verify that any forms that previously posted to index.php now correctly post to character_sheet.php
   - Confirm that form processing and data handling works as expected

4. Test with different user roles:
   - Log in as a regular player and test character viewing
   - Log in as an admin/storyteller and test character viewing
   - Verify that appropriate permissions are maintained

5. Test URL parameters:

3. For each page, add the footer include at the end of the file, before the closing HTML tag:

   ```php
   require_once 'includes/footer.php';
   ?>
   </body>

   ```

5. Update any page-specific title tags to work with the header include:
   - If the header.php uses a dynamic title, add a variable before including the header:
   ```php
   <?php
   $pageTitle = "Dashboard"; // Set page-specific title
   require_once 'includes/header.php';
   ?>
   ```

6. Test each page individually to ensure proper rendering with the new includes.

7. Verify that session handling and authentication still work correctly with the modified file structure.
